overview_raw: The Metal Fabricator Foundation program prepares students for a career dealing with the selection, layout, shearing, cutting, punching, drilling, forming, fitting and welding of steel plates and structural steel shapes into products for the forest, mining, construction, transportation and agricultural industries. Delivery: in person. See details . Typical projects that involve metal fabricators include bridges, buildings, hoppers, conveyors, towers, cranes, heavy-mining equipment, logging equipment, and ship parts and equipment. The Metal Fabricator Foundation program has General Admission intakes in September and March, as well as special intakes for High School cohorts in February through the High School Partnership Program . Please contact the Admissions Department for specific dates and registration. If you are interested in working in the marine and shipbuilding industry, you may be eligible to enter the Marine Fitter Apprenticeship program. Alternatively, if you are already indentured with Skilled Trades BC , or seeking more information on the apprenticeship itself, check out our Metal Fabricator Apprenticeship web page. The Program Basic theory and related information along with hands-on shop practice enable students to become competent in basic steel fabrication methods for products such as steel buildings, tanks and equipment. Good hand/eye coordination and good physical condition are desirable. Potential students with medical or physical difficulties should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview (telephone interview if out of town) with the institute’s rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963. entrance_requirements_raw: Scheduled intakes March and September each year. *Scheduled intakes are subject to change. Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. You must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements, we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Foundations of Math and Pre-Calculus 10 (50%) or Workplace Math 10 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Trades Discovery The Trades Discovery General and Trades Discovery for Women are full-time programs designed to prepare participants to successfully enter and complete a Trades Training program. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Please note that international students are not eligible to continue to an apprenticeship training program. To learn more about international student opportunities at BCIT, visit BCIT International . Study permit: A study permit is not required for programs with a duration of 6 months or less. Students may complete the program with a valid status in Canada for the duration of the program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. ( CIPC : 48.0511) Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. completion_requirements_raw: After completing the prescribed course work, all degree program students are required to complete an industry-sponsored project in their selected area.
program_details_raw: Program length 23 weeks, full-time Grading An overall minimum of 70% grade point average for the program and a minimum passing grade of 50% in all other courses are required to successfully complete the program. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC SkilledTradesBC BCIT transfers the student's name, contact information, Personal Education Number (PEN), and the name and date of the completed Foundation program to SkilledTradesBC. This information is used for the purposes of tracking successful completions in order to grant credit towards apprenticeship where applicable, and communicating with trainees to promote continuation in an apprenticeship program. courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Safe work practices follow a set of guidelines on how to perform specific tasks in the shop and should be observed whenever working in the shop to prevent hazards before they happen. In this course, students will learn the theoretical and practical components of what constitutes safe work practices, as outlined in the WorkSafeBC guidelines. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, you will learn how to use basic mathematics concepts and their use in metal fabrication such as, whole numbers, fractions, decimals, percentages, ratios, proportions, metric imperial conversions, Pythagoras Theorem, use of calculator, perimeter, area, volume basics. In addition, you will learn how to apply Geometric Line theory to develop parallel and intersecting lines for layout. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

Metal fabricators use blueprints and sketches and drawings during the fabrication process. In this course you will learn to identify basic lines, views and symbols from drawings. You will also learn to draw a detailed sketch and create a bill of materials based on information in a blueprint. As you work through the course you will use drawings to fabricate structural and plate projects. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1205

In this course, you will learn to identify and use metal fabrication hand and power tools such as grinders, drills, sanders, threaders, etc. Apply WorkSafeBC standards and regulations, shop specific standard operating procedures, and maintenance for all tools and equipment. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200

In this course you will learn to identify and use Metal Fabrication shop equipment during the fabrication of projects. Shop equipment includes plate shear, ironworker, plate rolls, band saws, pipe threader, brake press, and drill presses. You will also apply WorkSafeBC standards and regulations as well as shop specific standard operating procedures for use and maintenance of the equipment. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200

In this course you will learn to use drafting principles and applications in the Metal Fabrication industry. As you work through this course, you will engage in extensive lab work to apply triangulation and parallel line development techniques as well as the alphabet of lines (various kinds of lines) to create templates from blueprints. Parallel line development is a geometrical method of developing flat, two dimensional patterns for cylindrical and rectangular shaped objects. You will also learn the principles of the various types of pattern development. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210

In this course you will learn how to cut ferrous metals using oxy-fuel processes and non-ferrous metals with the plasma arc cutting processes. You will apply the theoretical concepts explained in the class in the practical projects to fabricate structural and plate components. This will include setting up oxy-fuel and plasma cutting equipment in order to cut, pierce and bevel various thickness of metal plate, cope structural shapes for fit-up, and use flame straightening. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200

This course introduces the fundamentals of arc welding, which includes the various welding processes, equipment, and accessories. The course provides hands-on shop training in SMAW (shielded metal arc welding) and GMAW (gas metal arc welding). As you work through the course, you will have many opportunities to use the various welding processes and equipment in the shop, under the supervision of the instructor. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200

This course introduces the basic principles of job specifications and blueprint reading. As you work through the course, you will study line types, isometric views, orthographic projections, dimensioning methods and general notes. Topics include using multi-page blueprints to locate information and solve problems in the shop, using shop drawings by correlating specifications and use math associated with blueprints. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1205

Plate development is a geometrical method of developing flat, two dimensional patterns for cylindrical and rectangular shaped objects. These objects can be in the form of piping, vessels, tanks, ducting, etc. In this course, you will learn to develop patterns using parallel and intersecting lines in the creation of templates for headers, branches, miters, tees, elbows, and copes and apply those templates to shop projects. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1240

This course covers the safe practices for lifting and moving objects, the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and the use of crane or hoist hand signals to direct movements of a load. In this course you will learn to apply math to calculate mass of structural shapes and plates in both imperial and metric units using the structural handbook and mass tables, calculate loads and tensions, center of balance, and identify rigging components to safely hoist and handle a load. Apply WorkSafeBC standards and regulations for loads being hoisted as well as the use of forklift, dollies, jacks, and rollers. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205

courses.prerequisite_raw: MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1215 and MTLF 1240
courses.course_overview_raw: Preparing metal surfaces for finishing requires attention to specification and adherence to quality standards. Metal products can be finished in a variety of methods, including galvanized, anodized and specialty epoxy finishes. In this course, you will learn how to apply codes and standards for finishing shop projects, including surface preparation and application of primers and paints. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1215 and MTLF 1240

courses.prerequisite_raw: MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1215 and MTLF 1220 and MTLF 1225 and MTLF 1230 and MTLF 1235 and MTLF 1240 and MTLF 1245
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, you will apply safe work practices to the fabrication of shop projects. The course will require integration of knowledge of shop tools and equipment, blueprint reading and interpretation as well as template development to fabricate a variety of shop projects, such as ring to ring, J hook, machine guard, mounting bracket, Jack stand, load divider, three-piece elbow complete with branch. The course also incorporates the production of a capstone project. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1215 and MTLF 1220 and MTLF 1225 and MTLF 1230 and MTLF 1235 and MTLF 1240 and MTLF 1245

courses.prerequisite_raw: MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1215 and MTLF 1240 and MTLF 1245
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, you will learn to identify and apply codes and standards encountered in the metal fabrication trade, interpret architectural information found on drawings, use measuring instruments to inspect finished products, describe different non-destructive testing methods, and use weld measuring equipment. Special focus will be on identification of weld discontinuities and the use of Liquid Penetrant Inspection, Magnetic Particle inspection, etc. Prerequisite(s): MTLF 1200 and MTLF 1205 and MTLF 1210 and MTLF 1215 and MTLF 1240 and MTLF 1245

LIBS 7001 and LIBS 7002 are mandatory plus 6.0 credits in accordance with BCIT Liberal Studies policy.
After completing the prescribed course work, all degree program students are required to complete an industry-sponsored project in their selected area.
Two years relevant work experience is a graduation requirement, not an entrance requirement.
